messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 and p95 latency SLO breaches detected in eu-west-1 for streaming endpoints after int8 calibration rollout. Auto-paging to #incidents. Initial signal at 2026-03-15T09:17:12Z (thread_ts=5298765432).

IncidentBot: Alerts summary: p95 > 450ms (target 200ms), p99 > 1200ms (target 600ms). Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate/stream. Error rate stable.

Ryan (oncall): taking initial ack, I'm oncall. Confirming I'm seeing the same spikes on the dashboard: p95 jumped ~2.5x, p99 ~2x. Streaming stall counts increased, streaming stalls correlate with dequantization errors in logs.

Meera (infra): I'm pulling infra telemetry now — kube nodes in eu-west-1 look healthy, GPU utilization up modestly but not saturated. There are increased queue backpressure metrics on the serving layer (queue_length).

Samir (runtime): latest int8 calibration rolled to eu-west-1 at 08:55 UTC (auto-rollout). The change set enabled int8 mixed-mode kernels for prefix caching. I suspect a calibration fallout that's increasing KV-cache miss handling overhead and dequant hops.

Alana (cs): We've got an incoming live support ping from a mid-market customer complaining about streamed responses breaking and long pauses. No 5xxs but UX broken for streaming apps. Customer: AcmePay in eu-west-1.

Ryan (oncall): Assigning severity: P1 for now due to customer impact + SLO breaches. Action plan: 1) Assess rollback/fallback options 2) Mitigate routing to fallback models 3) Notify CS + customers.

Samir (runtime): Quick mitigation options: - rollback calibration (revert to previous precision profile) OR - route traffic for streaming endpoints to fp16 variant or older int8 profile. Rolling rollback requires a config patch; can be applied to the control plane in ~6-8 minutes if no blockers.

Meera (infra): We can do route-level fallback with the router rule by updating the policy to route streaming requests to model:v2-fp16 for eu-west-1 only. Should be quick: updating route table + pushing new cache priming. I'll prepare the change.

Ryan (oncall): Do we have a safe rollback job? Samir, what's the safest path that minimizes warmup/latency penalties?

Samir (runtime): Safer path is routing to fp16 model variant rather than full rollback of calibration. Rollback may cause churn in other regions. Routing to fp16 keeps the int8 rollout in other regions intact. However fp16 has ~1.6x cost, but avoids stalls. We should do eu-west-1 only routing while we investigate calibration artifacts.

DeployBot: Deploy plan opened: change-id=CL-8843, diff: router rule add fallback-route(eu-west-1, /v1/* -> model:ancient-fp16-v2). Estimated deploy time: 4m.

Ryan (oncall): Meera, proceed with the route change. Samir will standby to monitor runtime metrics and look at any dequant errors. Alana, please notify AcmePay that we are investigating and may route them to a fallback model, expected impact: resolved streaming stalls, minor QoL diff.

Alana (cs): Notifying now. Message: "We're aware of streaming pauses in eu-west-1 and routing you to an alternate model to stabilize streaming while we investigate. Expect no request failures; you may see slightly different generation behavior. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

Meera (infra): Pushing router rule now. Command used:

```
# patch router policy for eu-west-1 streaming fallback
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/router/patch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","match":"/v1/chat/stream","route_to":"model:ancient-fp16-v2","reason":"mitigation-int8-calib-eu-west-1"}'
```

Meera (infra): Patch applied, propagation started. Warmup priming initiated for fp16 model in eu-west-1.

Samir (runtime): Watching logs. Dequant error stack traces drop immediately after rule propagation started. KV-cache miss handling decreased. Streaming stall counts trending down.

Ryan (oncall): Monitoring SLOs...

IncidentBot: Update: 3m after mitigation, p95 is down to 210ms, p99 down to 620ms (still slightly above target). Streaming stall rate decreased by 78%.

Ryan (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring for 30m. Samir - collect calibration logs and the int8 calibration table that was rolled; we need to replicate locally.

Samir (runtime): Copying relevant logs to /artifacts/incidents/5298765432/ and starting a dry-run of the int8 calibration in a canary cluster. I'm particularly looking at per-layer outlier scaling factors and attention KV dequant timing.

Meera (infra): Noting that other regions (us-west-2, ap-south) still on int8 roll but no anomalies reported. Looks eu-west-1-specific — maybe traffic pattern or seq-len distribution triggered an issuance.

Ryan (oncall): Alana, please follow up with AcmePay and any customers using streaming in eu-west-1, telling them we applied a routing mitigation and are investigating. Triage message should include ETA for root cause and a chance for a follow-up postmortem.

Alana (cs): Done. Sent message to affected customers and created a shared channel for AcmePay and CS if they want live updates.

CS-Liaison: Noted downstream internal ticket created with customer impact tags and SLA window start time.

Samir (runtime): Early hypothesis: int8 calibration created a micro-pattern where small repeated prefix requests cause KV eviction thrash leading to dequant overhead on streaming (stalls manifesting as long pauses rather than 5xx). Need to check calibration quant_scale edge entries.

Ryan (oncall): Action items: 1) Samir: collect calibration dump + run canary test (ETA 45m) 2) Meera: keep fallback route active for eu-west-1, prepare a safe rollback playbook if needed (ETA 20m) 3) Alana: customer comms and list of impacted tenants (ETA 10m) 4) Ryan: runbook + post-incident owner.

Samir (runtime): Added one-off log snippet for triage:

```
2026-03-15T08:56:12Z runtime::dequant WARN kv_dequant_latency=812ms model=ancient-int8-v3 layer=attn_kv scale=0.0039 note="scale outlier detected"
2026-03-15T08:56:12Z runtime::cache INFO kv_eviction reason=prefix_thrashing count=42 route=/v1/chat/stream
```

Samir (runtime): I'll upload the calibration table and a binary diff between the previous and current profiles to the incident folder.

Meera (infra): Current status: mitigation in effect, customer impacted flows routed to fp16, metrics improving, no widespread CPU/GPU saturation.

IncidentBot: Update: paging cleared from auto-pager at 09:25 UTC (page duration ~8m). On-call handover still active.

Ryan (oncall): I'll keep this thread open for root cause. If p99 stabilizes under 650ms for 30 minutes, we'll consider reducing urgency and schedule a postmortem. Samir, please include exact calibration delta and steps to reproduce.

Samir (runtime): Will do. Tentative root cause: an int8 calibration outlier entry that caused extra dequant and eviction thrash under streaming prefix-heavy workloads. If confirmed, fix will be a change to calibration algorithm to cap per-layer scale variance + a guarded rollout policy for streaming routes.

Alana (cs): Customers updated. No escalations yet. I'll keep CS channel open.

Ryan (oncall): Thanks all. Keep updates here. If anything changes escalate immediately with :rotating_light:.

Meera (infra): Logging the mitigation as "eu-west-1 streaming fallback route" in the incident tracker with change-id CL-8843 and timestamp.

IncidentBot: Incident status: mitgation=applied, impact=partial (streaming UX improved), severity=P1 -> monitoring.

Ryan (oncall): End of initial triage. Next updates: Samir uploads artifacts and canary results; Meera keeps route until we have RCA.

Samir (runtime): Uploads in progress. Starting local reproducer with seq-len distribution bumped to match AcmePay traces. Will post results within 45m.

Meera (infra): Standing by for rollback playbook if reproducer shows immediate repro in canary.

Alana (cs): Noted; I'll prepare a customer-suitable summary for the postmortem."
